title: Machine precondition
statement: Let $A$ be a program with $m$ registers, an oracle, a Boolean multi-tape Turing machine $D$, a choice of initial state for each decider, and a natural-number bound $B$. A configuration satisfies the precondition if, at a register-comparison instruction, the compared registers are distinct; at an input-payload comparison, the input has the corresponding valid encoding; and at a call instruction, the argument registers are distinct and $D$, started in the assigned state on the call’s encoded virtual input, halts with the oracle’s answer, leaves all work tapes blank with all work-tape heads at zero, and keeps every work-tape head within distance $B$ of zero throughout the run, including its halting time. Other configurations satisfy the precondition automatically.
caveat: The supplied statement does not include the definitions of the encoded virtual input, the compiled program, or the call-validity predicate, so their precise details cannot be rendered from this payload alone.
